Factual Position & Pleadings
1.

This Dar was filed on 12/10/2021 by Investigation Officer (Io) before this Tribunal in the
presence of the parties.
The Dar was prepared by Io in respect of a motor ve

hicular accident dated 12/10/2021 which took place in front of Monesty Market Outer Ring Road towards Wazirabad, Civil Lines, Delhi falling within the jurisdiction of PS Civil Lines in which one Sh. Sudesh Kumar Jha S/o Sh. Rajender (hereinafter referred to as "deceased") sustained fatal injuries.

As per PW-1, the deceased Sh. Sudesh Kumar Jha was her husband who died in the accident on 02/01/2020 at 09.00 P.M with a vehicle bearing registration no. DL-5SAZ-3114 (hereinafter referred to as "offending vehicle") which was driven by the R-1 in a very rash, negligent and careless manner and without blowing any horn or apply safety measures in a drunken condition and due to the fault of R-1 and the above mentioned offending vehicle fell down on the road and due to which the deceased sustained grievous injuries and he died on 21/01/2020.
It is further stated that deceased was 42 years old and was doing a private job and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month from his vocation.
An FIR No. 05/20/21 PS Civil Lines was registered by the police U/s 279/304A IPC.
Respondent is stated to be driver-cum- owner of the offending vehicle.
DAR was treated as a claim petition.
Respondent was directed to file his Written Statements.
2. A written statement was filed by respondent in which he declined the contents of the DAR.

PETITIONERS' EVIDENCE 4.

In support of their contentions, the petitioners examined Petitioner no. 1 Smt. Munni Devi, wife of the deceased, as PW-1. PW-1,vide her affidavit Ex. PW1/A, deposed that the deceased was her husband who lost his life on 21/01/2020 due to an accident dated 02/01/2020 involving the offending vehicle.
He further deposed that the accident took place due to the rashness and negligence of respondent.

He further deposed that deceased was 42 years old and was doing a private job and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month from his vocation and that the petitioners,
being the parents of the deceased, were completely dependent on the earnings of the deceased.

He relied upon the following documents:-

FINDINGS 6.
Oral submissions were advanced by Ld. Counsel for the parties.

7. I have perused the record and my issue wise findings are as under:-
" Whether the deceased Sh. Sudesh Kumar suffered fatal injuries in an accident that took place on 02.01.2020 at about 09.00 PM involving vehicle bearing registration No. DL-5SAZ-3114 owned and driven by the Respondent rashly and negligently?

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition Digitally MACT No. 745/21 Munni Devi & Ors.

In totality, the testimony of PW-1 seems reliable and worth acting upon.
Since, PW-1 has categorically stated that the deceased Sudesh Kumar Jha died as driver of the offending vehicle hit his motorcycle to the deceased.

10. It is not denied that R-1 was charge-sheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 279/304A IPC & 146/196 MV Act in the above FIR, which in itself is a strong circumstance to support the above oral testimony of PW-1 and the case of petitioners on this issue.

The copies of FIR, charge-sheet, site plan, Mechanical Inspection Report of the offending vehicle, Postmortem Report of deceased, Seizure Memo and Arrest Memo of respondent also corroborate the testimony of PW-1.
11.
In view of the above, it could be safely assumed that at the relevant time the deceased had died due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle being driven by respondent.
12. Having ruled so, this Tribunal now proceeds to assess the wrongful act, neglect or default of respondent, if any, in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
Admittedly, Respondent has not explained the circumstances under which the accident took place due to his rash and negligent driving.

In the absence of any evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the deceased, the only inference possible in the given facts and MACT No. 745/21 Munni Devi & Ors.
Vs. Nand Kishor Pathak

In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal is constrained to hold respondent guilty of gross neglect and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.

13. In view of the postmortem report pertaining to the deceased placed on record by the petitioners,
no dispute is left regarding the death of the deceased on account of injuries sustained by him in the above accident.
14. In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal holds that the deceased lost his life on account of neglect and default of respondent while driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
This issue thus stands decided against the respondent and in favour of the petitioners.

COMPENSATION 16.

The compensation to which the petitioners are entitled shall be under the following heads:-
(i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY 17.
In this regard, the petitioners have examined Petitioner No. 1 as PW1 who was the father of deceased.
PW-1 deposed that at the relevant time, the deceased was 42 years old and was doing a private job and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month from his vocation.
However, there is no material available on record which could corroborate the claim of PW-1 as to the monthly earnings of the deceased.

In the facts and circumstances, it would be appropriate to assess the monthly income of the deceased as per the minimum wages payable to an Unskilled-Person in Delhi at the time of accident i.e. 02/01/2020 were Rs.14,842- per month.
18. Petitioners have claimed that the deceased was aged about 42 years at the time of his death.
They have also placed on record a copy of Aadhar Card of the deceased as per which the date of birth of deceased was 05/01/1974.

opennyai_summary.facts:
An FIR No. 05/20/21 PS Civil Lines was registered by the police U/s 279/304A IPC.
DAR was treated as a claim petition.
opennyai_summary.issue:
1. Whether the deceased Sh. Sudesh Kumar suffered fatal injuries in an accident that took place on 02.01.2020 at about 09.00 PM involving vehicle bearing registration No. DL-5SAZ-3114 owned and driven by the Respondent rashly and negligently?
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
3.Relief.
7. I have perused the record and my issue wise findings are as under:-
" Whether the deceased Sh. Sudesh Kumar suffered fatal injuries in an accident that took place on 02.01.2020 at about 09.00 PM involving vehicle bearing registration No. DL-5SAZ-3114 owned and driven by the Respondent rashly and negligently?
14. In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal holds that the deceased lost his life on account of neglect and default of respondent while driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
"Whether the petitioners are entitled to any compensation, if so, to what amount and from whom?"
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition Digitally MACT No. 745/21 Munni Devi & Ors.
Vs. Nand Kishor Pathak Pagessigned PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:
2024.11.11 11:09:20 +0530 under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.
& Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
9.
Since, PW-1 has categorically stated that the deceased Sudesh Kumar Jha died as driver of the offending vehicle hit his motorcycle to the deceased.
In view of the above, it could be safely assumed that at the relevant time the deceased had died due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle being driven by respondent.
12. Having ruled so, this Tribunal now proceeds to assess the wrongful act, neglect or default of respondent, if any, in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
Admittedly, Respondent has not explained the circumstances under which the accident took place due to his rash and negligent driving.
In the absence of any evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the deceased, the only inference possible in the given facts and MACT No. 745/21 Munni Devi & Ors.
Vs. Nand Kishor Pathak
In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal is constrained to hold respondent guilty of gross neglect and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
13. In view of the postmortem report pertaining to the deceased placed on record by the petitioners,
no dispute is left regarding the death of the deceased on account of injuries sustained by him in the above accident.
However, there is no material available on record which could corroborate the claim of PW-1 as to the monthly earnings of the deceased.
The date of accident is MACT No. 745/21 Munni Devi & Ors. Vs. Nand Kishor Pathak
Going by the Aadhar Card of the deceased,
the age of deceased would be around 46 years as on the date of accident.
Hence, in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma &
Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr., (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been upheld by the Constitutional Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.
opennyai_summary.decision:
20. Irrespective of this, one fourth of the earnings of deceased shall be deducted towards his personal and living expenses in view of the law already discussed above.
This amount is awarded to the petitioners under this head.
United
, the petitioners are also held entitled to amounts of Rs. 20,000/- each under the heads of loss of estate and funeral expenses.
Further, in view of subsequent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of United India Insurance Company Ltd Vs Satinder Kaur & Ors MANU/HC/0500/2020 and The New India Assurance Company Ltd & Ors Vs Somwati & Ors MANU/HC/0674/2020, the petitioners are also entitled to compensation under the head "loss of consortium": -
Spousal Consortium : Rs.44,000/- (Rs. 44,000/- X 1)
Hence, the Petitioners are awarded a total sum of Rs.2,16,000/- (Rs.20,000/- + 20,000/- + Rs.
1,76,000/-) under this head.
The Petitioners are thus awarded a sum of Rs.23,86,643/- (Rupees Twenty three Lakhs Eighty Six Thousand Six Hundred and Forty Three Only) (Rs.21,70,643/- + Rs.2,16,000/-) along with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of filing of DAR i.e. 12/10/2021.
Since no interim compensation has been awarded, therefore no deduction is applicable.
25.1 Out of the awarded amount, Petitioner No. 1 is awarded a sum of Rs. 18,00,000/- (Rupees Eighteen Lakhs Only) and the said amount is directed to be kept with State Bank of India, Branch Tis Hazari Courts, New Delhi in MACAD in the form of 90 monthly fixed deposit receipts (FDRs)
payable in equal amounts for a period of 1 to 90 months in succession, as per the scheme formulated by Central Motor Vehicles (fifth Amendment) Rules, 2022 [(Directions at serial no. 35, 36 of Procedure for Investigation of Motor Vehicle Accidents (under Rule 150A)].
The amount of FDRs on maturity would be released in her savings/MACT Claims SB Account as and when she furnishes the details of her bank account which is near the place of her residence to the Bank Manager, State MACT No. 745/21 Munni Devi & Ors.
Out of the awarded amount, Petitioners No. 2 & 3 are awarded a sum of Rs.
2,40,000/- each (Rupees Two Lakhs Forty Thousand Only) and the said amount is directed to be kept with State Bank of India, Branch Tis Hazari Courts, New Delhi in MACAD in the form of 12 monthly fixed deposit receipts (FDRs) payable in equal amounts for a period of 1 to 12 months in succession, as per the scheme formulated by Central Motor Vehicles (fifth Amendment) Rules, 2022 [(Directions at serial no.
35, 36 of Procedure for Investigation of Motor Vehicle Accidents (under Rule 150A)].
The remaining amount of Rs.57,535/- (Rupees Fifty Seven Thousand Five Hundred and Thirty Five Only) is also directed to be released into her above said account, which can be withdrawn and utilized by the Petitioners no. 2 & 3 respectively.
